sources.title: Influence of Rising Water Temperature on the Temperate Seagrass Species Eelgrass (Zostera marina L.) in the Northeast USA
Northeast USA SeagrassNet Zm percent cover

response_independent_semantics.site_range: Northeast USA, New Hampshire to Maryland
response_independent_semantics.monitoring_period: site-specific annual records spanning 2003-2021; most sites 9-17 years
response_independent_semantics.site_design: three 50-m SeagrassNet transects along a depth gradient
response_independent_semantics.sampling: twelve 0.25 m2 quadrats per monitored transect
response_independent_semantics.quantitative_state: eelgrass percent cover on a near-continuous 0-100% scale
response_independent_semantics.coarse_state: absence when percent cover == 0; presence when percent cover > 0
response_independent_semantics.zero_is_ecological: The published hurdle analysis treats 0 cover as ecological absence, distinct from positive abundance.
response_independent_semantics.repeated_unit_evidence: Published models include site and quadrat as nested random effects, demonstrating repeated quadrat identity in the analysis dataset.
response_independent_semantics.published_data_scope: The Dryad modeling file supports published presence and abundance analysis; the present study asks a different temporal-memory question.

primary_overlap_warning.claim: external published matched panel; not fully independent biological replication

forbidden: Do not infer a different stable unit from response values.
Do not redefine zero after biological CSV access.
Do not call the panel fully independent from NPS/SeagrassNet evidence.
